name: base-tokenizedstocks API router
what_this_is: The data twin of manifest.json. manifest.json says where the documentation lives; this file says which endpoint answers which question. Match the user's question to a row's 'answers' patterns, then fetch. Route and fetch — do not load the whole file into reasoning.
how_to_route: STACK ROWS. One question usually needs several rows: 'is this implied dividend real' is the underlying price PLUS the dividend calendar PLUS the eligibility/custody terms. Never stop at the first row that matches.

Auth preference: a user-approved MCP or connected tool first, then a keyed API if a key is already in the environment, then keyless. Metered pay-per-call endpoints need the user's explicit yes before each paid call.

DATE THE OBSERVATION, NOT THE FETCH: equity price prints are delayed up to 15 minutes and quote the last session close on weekends, dividend calendars update on company announcements, issuer terms change without notice. Quote each number's own timestamp, and mark which are delayed.

HONESTY FLAGS ARE LOAD-BEARING: rows marked 'no-live-venue' describe infrastructure that does not exist in production yet (as of 2026-09-06). Compute from them only hypothetically, and say so in the answer.

THE SUBJECT IS BASE: routes pointing at off-Base products (multiplier-history) are evidence anchors about the class — use them to prove what a mechanism looks like when it actually fires, never to price or recommend a position.
Execution is absent by design: no swap routers, no transaction builders, no order endpoints. This skill is read-only.
Re-verify liveness on first use in a session: free endpoints drift, geo-block, or change shape.

answers: has the dividend mechanism actually fired for this token
is the multiplier above 1.0
when did corporate events activate onchain
evidence that a dividend reached token holders
routes.example: GET /api/v2/public/assets/AAPLx/multiplier?network=Solana — current multiplier plus any pending activation; GET /api/v2/public/assets/AAPLx/multiplier/history?page=0&pageSize=20&network=Solana — dated activation log: reason (Dividend / split types), previous→current multiplier, activation timestamp
routes.notes: The print-evidence route: the one keyless endpoint that answers 'did it actually happen' with a dated log. xStocks only (Backed's active line, off-Base) — Dinari publishes no per-payment equivalent, so on Base the record stays terms-plus-session-check. The API is issuer-operated, so a verified print needs the onchain leg too: EVM — eth_call getCurrentMultiplier() (selector 0x2b63c300; returns multiplier as an 1e18 mantissa, a pending flag, and an event counter that should equal the history length; same contract address reused across xStocks' EVM deployments, resolvable via /api/v2/public/assets/{SYMBOL}?network=...); Solana — the Scaled UI Amount extension in token metadata (Solscan); TON — get_display_multiplier. Verified working 2026-09-07. Expect activation timestamps near but not exactly at the documented 00:30 UTC day-after-ex-date (observed 23:55–04:00); a multiplier above 1.0 on a dividend payer is the exercised print, and the increments are reinvestment net of withholding, not gross yield. Evidence anchor, not a venue: xStocks does not deploy on Base — this route proves the class's dividend pipe can fire onchain; it never prices or monitors a Base position (on Base, the dividend arrival checks are the USD+ distribution transaction and the B20 multiplier read — the b20-multiplier route; see corporate-action.md). Liveness re-check 2026-09-10: HTTP 200; AAPLx log unchanged (5 dividend activations, latest 2026-08-08, multiplier 1.003269).

answers: has a corporate action or dividend actually fired on a Coinbase B20 stock
is the B20 multiplier above 1.0

routes.example: POST / with eth_call {"to": <B20 token>, "data": "0x1b3ed722"} — multiplier() returns the WAD-scaled factor (divide by 1e18). Token addresses resolve from the docs.base.org tokenized-stocks registry (onchain registry 0x3f3E8cf41cdd3b1D118c16471aB0113DfDDd5CaD); 13 live tokens as of 2026-09-07 (AAPLc, AMZNc, COINc, CRCLc, GOOGLc, INTCc, METAc, MSFTc, MSTRc, NVDAc, SNDKc, SPCXc, TSLAc)
routes.notes: THE BASE-NATIVE PRINT CHECK. B20 converts dividends to underlying shares through the multiplier, never cash ('cash dividends are converted to shares of the underlying equity and reflected via a multiplier update' — docs.base.org); a multiplier above 1e18 means the pipe fired. Verified sweep 2026-09-07: all 13 live tokens read exactly 1.0, including AAPLc, GOOGLc, METAc, and MSFTc, which have passed several quarterly ex-dates since launch — the mechanism is documented but has never exercised. Re-run after any ex-date; the absence itself is the finding. History lives in MultiplierUpdated events; scaledBalanceOf(address) (selector 0x1da24f3e) reads raw balance × multiplier. Batch reads trip official-RPC rate limits — pace the calls or alternate endpoints (base-rpc.publicnode.com). Liveness re-check 2026-09-10: mainnet.base.org RPC HTTP 200 (eth_blockNumber).

routes.example: GET /api/v2/networks/base/tokens/{contract_address} — price and liquidity pools for an ERC-20/B20 token on Base; resolve the contract address from the issuer docs first
routes.notes: Rate-limited public API. This prices a tokenized stock on Base (a Dinari dShare, a Coinbase B20, or an ST0x wrapper like wtNVDA), not strip legs. Contract addresses live with the issuer (manifest rows dinari-dshares, coinbase-stocks, basestonk-launchpad); do not guess addresses. Verified response shape 2026-09-08: price_usd, total_reserve_in_usd, normalized_total_supply (the onchain float), and relationships under top_pools (NOT pools). Verify the token by address, never by symbol — AAPLc displays as 'AAPL' on GeckoTerminal. An empty result is a finding, not a void: dShares trade on Dinari's order sessions (not permissionless DEX pools), so a dNVDA search returns empty by design; only 4 of 13 B20 trade in live pools at all (NVDAc, GOOGLc, AAPLc, METAc per docs.basestonk.io/stock-pairs.md, 2026-09-08). Thin liquidity here is itself a finding (gap-menu entry #3). For baskets: this row is the exit-depth check per constituent — the rebalance is gated by the thinnest pool, not the average (index-composition.md, Part A). Pair with the underlying-price route to compute the onchain basis (onchain-basis route; references/onchain-basis.md). Liveness re-check 2026-09-10: HTTP 200; wtNVDA read returned price_usd / total_reserve_in_usd / normalized_total_supply / top_pools — shape unchanged.

routes.example: implied forward dividend = (YT price × periods per year) / underlying price — YT price from the strip venue (NONE LIVE as of 2026-09-06), underlying from underlying-price route
routes.notes: NO-LIVE-VENUE FLAG: no production PT/YT market for tokenized equities exists on any chain as of 2026-09-06 (Pendle verified absent). answers: is the token at a premium to the share
why doesn't the token price match the stock
how far is the onchain token from the underlying
does the wrapper track the real stock
what is the basis between token and share
routes.example: basis = (token_price_usd / underlying_price) - 1, expressed as a percentage — token_price from the token-price route (GeckoTerminal token endpoint, price_usd), underlying from the underlying-price route (Yahoo v8 chart, meta.regularMarketPrice). Stamp each leg with its OWN timestamp and name the equity leg's session state (open / pre-open / closed-holiday / closed-weekend).
routes.notes: Verified working 2026-09-08 against the four B20 books that trade live (NVDAc, GOOGLc, AAPLc, METAc) plus wtNVDA. Pitfalls that make a basis read wrong if skipped: (1) the two legs print on different clocks — the onchain leg trades 24/7, the equity leg quotes the last close on weekends and market holidays (the 2026-09-08 set was read against a Friday close because Monday was Labor Day); a basis measured against a stale print is flow-only information, never mispricing. (2) GeckoTerminal's token endpoint returns price_usd, total_reserve_in_usd, normalized_total_supply (the float), and relationships under top_pools (NOT pools) — verify the token by address, never by symbol: AAPLc displays as 'AAPL'. (3) A wrapper carries its own basis against its native counterpart (wtNVDA vs NVDAc, -0.25% on 2026-09-08) on a far thinner book; read both spreads when a wrapper is in play. (4) An empty GeckoTerminal result is not an absence of product — dShares trade on Dinari's order sessions, not on permissionless DEX pools, so a dNVDA search returns empty by design. The four-entry decomposition that explains a basis (session gap, depth/float, arb-access asymmetry, stacked legs) lives in references/onchain-basis.md; the per-issuer comparison frame that uses the basis as one row lives in references/issuer-comparison.md. Basis is NOT the strip premium (different leg of R_total) and NOT a dividend signal. Liveness re-check 2026-09-10: both legs re-verified (token-price 200; underlying-price via stockanalysis fallback 200).

Dinari handles brokerage, settlement, custody, and compliance itself; that consolidation is part of the claim stack. In any lending context the same question applies to the lender's recovery address — an ineligible recipient of seized collateral holds a broken remedy (future-yield-lending.md, entry 1). routes.example: GET /api/v2/networks/base/tokens/{B20-contract}/pools — enumerates every pool containing the registered stock token in one call; attributes: name, dex, pool_created_at, volume_usd{h24,h6,h1}, transactions{h24,h6,h1}{buys,sells}, price_change_percentage{h24,h6,h1}, reserve_in_usd, fdv_usd; include=base_token,quote_token resolves the meme leg's contract. Browser User-Agent required.
routes.notes: THE VERIFICATION ROUTE for the meme-pair genre: enumerating by registry token address guarantees the stock leg is the genuine B20 contract by construction — name search does not (display names drift; 'AAPL' pairs exist on Robinhood Chain and BSC under other issuers' real tokens). Verified live 2026-09-07 (~30 pools across NVDAc/SPCXc/AAPLc; o1-launchpad dominant, bankr secondary). Also the TRENDING SCREEN route: split the stock's own books (USDC/WETH legs) from the meme pairs, then rank memes on momentum (volume_usd.h24 primary, h6 share vs a uniform ~25% as acceleration), flow skew (transactions buys vs sells), depth (reserve_in_usd), and age/stage (pool_created_at vs the swarm window; check graduation). Two display corrections from the 2026-09-07 live pull: depth reads come from reserve_in_usd — populated on o1 hook pools (an earlier 'null reserves' note was a wrong-key read; there is no reserve_usd attribute) — and fdv_usd is unusable for meme legs (read $16.7M then $2.97M hours later on the same pool, and near-identical across all meme pools, tracking the stock side). The 0xb200-prefix vanity-squat print lives in meme-pair-launchpad.md. WRAPPER BLIND SPOT (found in the 2026-09-07 degen dogfood): enumerating by the B20 registry address catches only NATIVE stock legs. A second surface pairs memes against wrapped stock tokens — the ST0x family (wtCOIN, wtNVDA, wtMSTR, wtSPCX and seven more; wtCOIN = 'Wrapped Coinbase Global Inc ST0x' at 0x5cDa0E1CA4ce2af96315f7F8963C85399c172204, verified onchain): on the day COINc-native showed zero pools, BALD/wtCOIN traded ~$247k. Cover the wrapped surface by searching the wrapped symbol or the launchpad's own API (basestonk-launches route); a wt* leg is neither fake nor the registry token — a separate claim stack to walk (wrapper issuer, 1:1 backing, its own custody). Also: pool-count censuses via the dex endpoint DO paginate with an explicit ?page= even when links.next is null. Liveness re-check 2026-09-10: HTTP 200.

answers: what launched on the BaseStonk launchpad
how many tokens has a launchpad deployed
which launchpad launches against tokenized stocks
per-launch hook and generation data (v1-v6, b20 rail)
routes.example: GET /api/launchpad/tokens?chain=base&pair=stocks&sort=trending — every launch with pair, hook, price, market cap, volume, holders and tax; filters: sort (trending|age|marketcap|volume|holders), q, pair (address or crypto|memes|stocks), generation (v1..v6|simple|b20), addresses (watchlist up to 50). Plus /tokens/{addr}/pressure (buys/sells/volume/wallets over 5m/1h/4h/24h), /candles, /trades, /holders.
routes.notes: Verified 2026-09-07 (docs.basestonk.io/integration/api.md; live endpoint exercised 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200; 506 launches returned, hasNext=true)). BaseStonk is a launchpad NOT named in Base's official B20 ecosystem announcement — the official list is non-exhaustive, which is itself the lesson. Distinctive mechanics: every launch is a live Uniswap v4 pool from block one (no bonding curve, no graduation, no migration), the launcher must end every launch holding nothing, no admin key over any pool; B20-native launches run through a separate launcher+hook (generation=b20). Its 'dividend baskets' are platform trade-fee dividends, NOT equity dividends — same word, different claim. The chain=robinhood side (Robinhood's own 194 stock tokens) is off-Base evidence, never a venue. Rate limits: 120 units/min per IP, cost-weighted; a 429 is refused, never empty.
